meta.mechanism: CETP modulator/inhibitor (weak; raises HDL-C, no meaningful LDL-C/apoB lowering)
meta.indication: secondary prevention after recent acute coronary syndrome

n_randomized.quote: We randomly assigned 15,871 patients who had had a recent acute coronary syndrome to receive the CETP inhibitor dalcetrapib, at a dose of 600 mg daily, or placebo
n_randomized.note: Registry (S3) also lists enrollment 15871 ACTUAL. Table 2: placebo N=7933, dalcetrapib N=7938.

median_followup.quote: Patients were followed for a median of 31 months.

primary_endpoint.value: Composite of death from coronary heart disease, nonfatal myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, unstable angina, or cardiac arrest with resuscitation
primary_endpoint.quote: The primary efficacy end point was a composite of death from coronary heart disease, nonfatal myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, unstable angina, or cardiac arrest with resuscitation.

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Age >=45 y, hospitalized for ACS; randomized 4-12 weeks after the index ACS; no HDL-C entry limits; LDL-C managed per evidence-based care
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: Patients 45 years of age or older who provided written informed consent were eligible to participate if they had been hospitalized for an acute coronary syndrome characterized by elevated cardiac biomarkers, with symptoms of acute myocardial ischemia, ischemic electrocardiographic abnormalities that were new or presumed to be new, or loss of viable myocardium on imaging.
inclusion_key_criteria.note: Timing and HDL criteria from design paper S2 abstract: 'beginning 4 to 12 weeks after an index ACS event. There are no prespecified boundaries for HDL cholesterol levels at entry.'

planned_events.quote: We projected that with 1600 primary end-point events, the study would have 90% power to detect a 15% reduction in the relative risk of an event with dalcetrapib as compared with placebo
planned_events.note: Design paper S2 abstract: 'The trial will continue until 1,600 primary end point events have occurred'.

assumed_rrr.quote: We projected that with 1600 primary end-point events, the study would have 90% power to detect a 15% reduction in the relative risk of an event with dalcetrapib as compared with placebo, assuming an average baseline HDL cholesterol level of 40 mg per deciliter (1.0 mmol per liter) and an increase of approximately 11 mg per deciliter (0.3 mmol per liter) with dalcetrapib.
assumed_rrr.note: The assumed 15% RRR was justified by an HDL-C increase of ~11 mg/dL, i.e. the design rested entirely on the HDL hypothesis.

power.quote: the study would have 90% power to detect a 15% reduction in the relative risk

alpha.note: NOT FOUND in the NEJM main text (no 'two-sided' statement located); likely in the supplementary appendix / protocol, which were not opened.

stopped_early.quote: At the second prespecified interim analysis, which included 1135 primary end-point events (71% of those projected), the independent data and safety monitoring board recommended termination of the trial for futility, in accordance with prespecified criteria (see the Supplementary Appendix).
stopped_early.note: Stopped for futility at 1135/1600 planned events (71%). Interim analyses were planned at ~800 and ~1120 events. Final adjudicated primary events after close-out: 1289 (656 + 633). Public announcement: Roche release 7 May 2012 (S4).

baseline.quote: the mean low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol level was 76 mg per deciliter (2.0 mmol per liter)
At the time of randomization, the mean HDL cholesterol level was 42 mg per deciliter (1.1 mmol per liter)
the mean apolipoprotein B level was 81 mg per deciliter
the mean apolipoprotein A1 level was 137 mg per deciliter

biomarker_effects.timepoint: over the course of the trial
biomarker_effects.quote: Over the course of the trial, HDL cholesterol levels increased from baseline by 4 to 11% in the placebo group and by 31 to 40% in the dalcetrapib group.
biomarker_effects.note: Reported only as from-baseline ranges by arm (dalcetrapib +31 to +40%, placebo +4 to +11%); no single placebo-adjusted figure given. Implied placebo-adjusted difference roughly +25 to +30 points (curator inference, not reported).

biomarker_effects.timepoint: over the course of the trial
biomarker_effects.quote: Dalcetrapib had a minimal effect on LDL cholesterol levels.
biomarker_effects.note: No number given in text (Figure 1 only).

biomarker_effects.quote: Apolipoprotein A1 levels were increased by 10% after 3 months of treatment with dalcetrapib and by 9% at the end of the trial (P<0.001), with a minimal effect on levels of apolipoprotein B.
biomarker_effects.note: apoB effect described only as 'minimal'; no number in main text.

biomarker_effects.quote: Apolipoprotein A1 levels were increased by 10% after 3 months of treatment with dalcetrapib and by 9% at the end of the trial (P<0.001)
Dalcetrapib increased placebo-corrected HDL-C by 25, 27, and 31% at weeks 4, 12, and 36, respectively
Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels did not change.
biomarker_effects.note: Full text: 'A small, but significant decrease in LDL-C of 4% (P < 0.05) was observed at week 4 only.'

biomarker_effects.quote: Placebo-corrected apolipoprotein B100 decreased significantly by 4, 3, and 5% at weeks 4, 24, and 36 ( P < 0.05; Figure 4 ).
After 4, 24, and 36 weeks of treatment with dalcetrapib, CETP activity decreased by 51, 53, and 56% (placebo corrected, all P < 0.0001)
Dalcetrapib mean percent changes from baseline relative to placebo were +26·9% (90% CI 20·0–33·9%) for HDL-C and +6·8% (2·5–11·1) for apolipoprotein A1.
Dalcetrapib increased high-density lipoprotein cholesterol by up to 36% and apolipoprotein A-I by up to 16%.
biomarker_effects.note: Pooled phase IIa/IIb doses 300-900 mg; 'up to' value, adjustment not specified in abstract.

hr.quote: hazard ratio with dalcetrapib, 1.04; 95% confidence interval, 0.93 to 1.16; P=0.52

events_treatment.note: Read from Table 2 image: dalcetrapib (N=7938) primary end point 656 (8.3%). Text: 'which occurred in 8.3% of the patients in the dalcetrapib group'.

events_control.note: Read from Table 2 image: placebo (N=7933) primary end point 633 (8.0%).

safety_signals.quote: the mean systolic blood pressure was 0.6 mm Hg higher with dalcetrapib as compared with placebo (P<0.001 for both comparisons)
The median C-reactive protein level was 0.2 mg per liter higher

safety_signals.value: No DSMB safety signal at stop
safety_signals.quote: No safety signals relating to the dal-OUTCOMES trial were reported from the DSMB.

safety_signals.note: Read from Table 2 image: death from any cause dalcetrapib 226 (2.8%) vs placebo 229 (2.9%), HR 0.99 (0.82-1.19). Registry S3 also lists 226 vs 229.

genetics.finding: CETP TaqIB variant: B2B2 carriers have higher HDL-C and lower CAD risk; association lost after adjusting for HDL-C (individual-patient meta-analysis, 13,677 subjects).
genetics.quote: TaqIB genotype was significantly associated with the risk of CAD (odds ratio=0.78 [0.66 to 0.93]) in B2B2 individuals compared with B1B1 individuals (P for linearity=0.008). Additional adjustment for HDL-C levels rendered a loss of statistical significance (P=0.4).

genetics.finding: Common CETP variants (TaqIB, I405V, -629C>A) that modestly lower CETP activity and raise HDL-C are weakly associated with lower coronary risk (meta-analysis, 27,196 cases).
genetics.effect: per-allele OR for coronary disease 0.95 (0.92-0.99) for TaqIB
genetics.quote: The combined per-allele odds ratios (ORs) for coronary disease were 0.95 (95% CI, 0.92-0.99) for TaqIB, 0.94 (95% CI, 0.89-1.00) for I405V, and 0.95 (95% CI, 0.91-1.00) for -629C>A.

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization: genetically raised HDL-C (LIPG Asn396Ser; 14-SNP HDL score) does not lower MI risk; LDL score does.
genetics.effect: LIPG 396Ser OR 0.99 (0.88-1.11); HDL genetic score OR per 1 SD 0.93 (0.68-1.26)
genetics.quote: However, a 1 SD increase in HDL cholesterol due to genetic score was not associated with risk of myocardial infarction (OR 0·93, 95% CI 0·68-1·26, p=0·63).

genetics.finding: Rare CETP protein-truncating variants (1 in 975 carriers) raise HDL-C, lower LDL-C and triglycerides, and are associated with lower CHD risk.
genetics.quote: CETP PTV carrier status was associated with reduced risk for CHD (summary odds ratio, 0.70; 95% confidence interval, 0.54-0.90; P=5.1×10-3).

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization: CETP genetic score lowers CV risk in proportion to apoB reduction; on a statin (HMGCR) background the apoB reduction and the risk reduction are attenuated, so benefit tracks apoB, not LDL-C or HDL-C.
genetics.effect: CETP score alone OR 0.946 (0.921-0.972); combined with HMGCR score OR 0.985 (0.955-1.015)
genetics.quote: When combined with the HMGCR score, the CETP score was associated with the same reduction in LDL-C levels but an attenuated reduction in apoB levels and a corresponding attenuated nonsignificant risk of major cardiovascular events (OR, 0.985 [95% CI, 0.955-1.015]).

consensus_explanation.summary: Dalcetrapib is a weak CETP modulator that raised HDL-C by ~30% but did not lower LDL-C, non-HDL-C or apoB. The field's accepted reading is that (1) raising HDL-C per se is not causally protective (Mendelian randomization, Voight 2012; null HDL-raising trials) and (2) the benefit of CETP inhibition is driven by, and proportional to, reduction of apoB-containing lipoproteins (Ference 2017; REVEAL). With no apoB lowering, no benefit was expected. Tall & Rader attribute REVEAL's success relative to dalcetrapib to potency. The trial tested the wrong mechanism (HDL hypothesis) with a drug lacking the causal (apoB) effect; CETP as a target was later partly validated by REVEAL, so 'drug_or_dose' is chosen over 'target'. Post hoc pharmacogenomics (ADCY9 genotype) proposed a responder subgroup, tested later in dal-GENE.

pre_readout.note: readout_date 2012-05-07 (Roche release). Sources with pub_date before that date are listed as available.
available_before_readout: Design: N ~15,600, 1600 events, ACS population, endpoints (S2, 2009-12; abstract only - power/RRR not in abstract)
Phase 2: dal-PLAQUE (S6, 2011-09-09): HDL-C +26.9% placebo-adjusted at 24 mo; imaging no harm
Phase 2: dal-VESSEL (S5, 2012-02-16): HDL-C +25-31%, LDL-C unchanged, apoB -3 to -5%, no BP effect, no FMD improvement
Phase 2 pooled (S7, 2009-07-01): HDL-C up to +36%, no BP or aldosterone signal
Genetics: CETP variants weakly protective (Boekholdt 2005 S13; Thompson 2008 S8)
Class precedent: torcetrapib ILLUMINATE harm (2006-12) and HDL-raising niacin/fibrate null trials (not curated here)
only_after_readout: Voight 2012 HDL Mendelian randomization (S9, 2012-05-17 - 10 days after readout)
